_supersedes: earlier training.json draft — this is the authoritative extraction
_measured:
Loads come from the MacroFactor workout log export (2026-09-09), which records weight, reps and RIR per set for the sessions of 2026-08-05, 08-07, 08-22 and 08-25. That export supersedes the earlier note claiming these were read off the machines on 2026-08-29: those numbers disagreed with what he actually logged, and two of them were plainly swapped — the plan had row 42.5 / pulldown 21.25 where the log has row ~22 / pulldown ~40, and 21.25 x 2 = 42.5. Rear delt fly was 6.8 in the plan against 16-20 logged. Lateral raise at 5 kg/arm is the one value both sources agreed on.

Caveats kept deliberately: the logged weight is the stack selection, not the force at the handle, so it does not convert to a Rayofi setting. Where a logged set fell short of the prescribed rep range — pulldown at 11 reps for a 12-15 target, rear delt at 11 for a 15 target — the load here is the logged one and will need coming down slightly to hit the range at RIR 2. Chest press, triceps pushdown, hip thrust and leg press have no entry in this export window and keep their earlier numbers, unverified.

philipp.goal: K-idol taper · fat loss · muscle retention

locationNotes.gym: Holmes Place · cable tower + machines. All primary exercises run on the cable tower — constant tension, exact progression.
locationNotes.home: Everything at home runs on the Rayofi Go-Tone Pro: motor-controlled resistance from 3 to 30 kg, dialled in rather than stacked, anchored to a doorframe, a chair, or your own foot. One quick-attach handle ships with it; the second is for the two-handed moves. There is only one unit, so anything that would be a wide-bar two-hand pull at the gym goes one arm at a time here, and the rep counts say so. Rayofi's manual gives no anchor height per exercise — their videos do, worth watching once per new movement.
locationNotes.travel: The Rayofi Go-Tone Pro is the entire travel kit — under a kilo, anchors to any door. Same one-unit rules as at home: the pulls go one arm at a time, and the second handle covers the two-handed moves.

fullBody.title: Full Body
fullBody.focus: side delt · lat · chest · back · rear delt · legs + core maintenance
fullBody.note: Same session both gym days. Nine exercises to keep it near an hour — face pull, biceps curl, hamstring curl and the cable crunch are the ones left out; add any of them back if the hour has room.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Fresh first — the most important move for the look. Constant tension at the bottom, where a dumbbell would give you none. Arm slightly bent, lead with the elbow to shoulder height. Goal: a clean 15, then 6 kg.

exercises.name: Wide Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Second most important taper muscle after the side delt. Pull the bar to the upper chest, feel the lats, controlled on the way back. Replaces the pull-up you cut — that would have thickened the upper traps and shortened the neckline.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press (high-to-low)
exercises.cue: Anchor high, stand away from the tower, press forward and downward in front of the chest. The downward angle hits the upper chest automatically — the athletic line under the collarbone.

exercises.name: Cable Row (neutral)
exercises.cue: Sit upright, handle to the belly, elbows close to the body, shoulder blades together. Builds posture without thickening the neck — stay moderate, don't heave.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly (Cable)
exercises.cue: Gives the shoulder depth and the 3D look without mass. Arms almost straight, lead with the little fingers, squeeze the rear delts together.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.cue: Elbows fixed at your sides, pull the rope apart at the bottom, brief hold. A defined arm, not mass.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust (Dumbbell or Sandbag)
exercises.cue: Maintenance — hold, don't build. Shoulders against a bench, the weight across the hips, full hip extension, 1s hold at the top.

exercises.name: Leg Press (light)
exercises.cue: Maintenance — hold, don't build. High reps, light weight, never progress. Keeps the legs lean and defined without making them thicker.

exercises.name: Hollow Hold
exercises.cue: Lower back flat on the floor, arms long. Builds the deep abdominal tension that visually tightens the waist.

solo.title: eGym
solo.focus: full body — eGym sets the resistance
solo.note: Always eGym on Mondays. The machines pick and adjust resistance themselves, so there's nothing to plan a load, set count or RIR for here.

exercises.name: eGym
exercises.cue: Whatever the eGym circuit is that day — machine-guided, full body.

rain.title: Full Body — Rayofi
rain.day: Home · rain stand-in for Tue/Wed or Sun
rain.focus: side delt · lat · upper back · chest · glutes
rain.note: Your gym days are Tue (Wed on conference weeks) and Sun; this is the home version for the days the weather stops the trip. Six exercises, not nine: the triceps pushdown, the light squat and the hollow hold came out because the press already loads the triceps, the gym leg press and the walking already cover the legs, and a core hold does not need a slot in a session you are short of time for. What is left is the four taper drivers, the chest press and one posterior movement. Order is grouped by anchor height, and the rear delt pull-apart needs no anchor at all, so it runs inside the row's rest. If even this is too much, the first three are the session — everything after them is a bonus. Loads are starting positions from your own logged cable sets.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lateral Raise (one arm)
exercises.cue: Fresh first — the taper driver. Lead with the elbow to shoulder height, constant tension. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lat Pulldown (kneeling, one arm)
exercises.cue: Anchor high, kneel, pull the elbow down and out, squeeze the lat. Only one Rayofi, so this is one arm at a time — both sides make one set. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Row (one arm)
exercises.cue: Upright, pull the elbow to the ribs, shoulder blades together, no swing. Only one Rayofi, so this is one arm at a time — both sides make one set. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Rear Delt Pull-Apart
exercises.cue: Both handles on the one cable — arms almost straight, apart to the chest, lead with the little fingers. Runs inside the row's rest — no anchor needed, so nothing to rebuild.

exercises.name: Rayofi Chest Press
exercises.cue: Anchor low behind you, stand away from the anchor, press forward and slightly down in front of the chest.

exercises.name: Rayofi Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Maintenance — hold, don't build. Cable over the hips, shoulders supported, full extension, 1s at the top.

optional.title: Optional Extras
optional.day: Any free solo morning — not scheduled
optional.focus: taper accessories · shoulder health · low fatigue cost
optional.note: Not scheduled and not required — for the mornings you have free alone, outside Tue/Wed, Fri and Sun. Deliberately light (RIR 3, short) so it never eats into recovery for those three: mostly what Full Body leaves out for time, plus a little more of your #1 taper driver. Skip it whenever the morning doesn't happen; nothing downstream depends on it. Loads unset — the Rayofi is untested for these. Loads are starting positions, not measured on the device: his come from his own logged cable sets in August, hers are deliberately low because there is no workout export for her at all. Dial to whatever makes the prescribed reps land at the target RIR, then write the real number in.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lateral Raise (one arm)
exercises.cue: Optional top-up on the #1 taper driver — only if the morning is actually free, not a make-up session. One handle, switch sides between sets. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Biceps Curl (one arm)
exercises.cue: Trimmed from Full Body for time. One handle, elbow fixed, slow on the way down. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Ankle-Strap Hamstring Curl
exercises.cue: Trimmed from Full Body for time. Ankle strap on, cable anchored low behind you, curl the heel towards the glute.

exercises.name: Rayofi Face Pull
exercises.cue: Trimmed from Full Body for time. Both handles on the one cable — elbows high and wide, hands past the ears, the counterpart to all the pressing.

exercises.name: Rayofi Kneeling Crunch
exercises.cue: Trimmed from Full Body for time. Anchor high, kneeling, fold the ribs towards the hips.

rain.title: Full Body — Rayofi
rain.focus: glutes first, then back and shoulder
rain.note: Your gym day is Monday on the eGym, which sets its own resistance and cannot be copied at home — this is the manual version for the days the weather stops the trip. Seven exercises, not nine: the rear delt fly and the dead bug came out, because the row and the pulldown already work the back of the shoulder and a core hold is the easiest thing to do outside a session. Glutes stay first because that is the priority, then it is grouped by anchor height to save re-anchoring the one unit. The push-up needs no equipment, so it runs inside the row's rest. If time collapses, the hip thrust and the pulldown are the session. Loads are deliberately low starting points — there is no workout export for you — so climb from them.

exercises.name: Rayofi Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: First — glutes are the priority. Cable over the hips, shoulders supported, squeeze 2s at the top.

exercises.name: Rayofi Squat (wide)
exercises.cue: Feet wider than shoulders, knees tracking out, 3s down. Inner thigh plus glutes.

exercises.name: Rayofi Ankle-Strap Hamstring Curl
exercises.cue: Ankle strap on, cable anchored low behind you, curl the heel towards the glute, controlled back. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lateral Raise (one arm)
exercises.cue: The shoulder that makes the waist look narrower. Lead with the elbow. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Row (one arm)
exercises.cue: Upright, elbow to the ribs, shoulder blades together. Only one Rayofi, so this is one arm at a time — both sides make one set. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Push-Up (knee or standard)
exercises.cue: No equipment. Knee version to regress, 3s down. Chest and triceps in one. Runs inside the row's rest — no equipment, so no rebuild.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lat Pulldown (kneeling, one arm)

fri.title: Shared Session
fri.focus: same exercises · own resistance · swap during rest
fri.note: Five exercises, and nobody stands still. One Rayofi, one exercise at a time: his set, her set, his set is her rest. Two things break that pattern on purpose — the hip thrust is hers alone (her priority, and his plan holds the legs rather than builds them), and the rear delt pull-apart needs no anchor, so each of you does it while the other is on the device. Everything that is a wide-bar two-hand pull at the gym is one arm at a time here, sides back to back, rep counts per side. Loads are starting positions, not measured on the device — his from his own logged cable sets, hers deliberately low because there is no export for her.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lateral Raise (one arm)
exercises.cue: Already one-arm even at the gym cable tower. Lead with the elbow to shoulder height, constant tension. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Hers alone. Glutes are her priority and his plan holds the legs rather than building them, so while she works her three sets he does the rear delt pull-apart beside her — no anchor needed, nobody waits. He still gets hip extension on Tue and Sun at the gym.

exercises.name: Rayofi Rear Delt Pull-Apart
exercises.cue: Both handles on the one cable — apart to the chest, lead with the little fingers. This one needs no anchor, so it is what each of you does while the other is on the Rayofi: he during her hip thrusts, she during his pulls. It never costs the session a slot of its own.

exercises.name: Rayofi Row (one arm)
exercises.cue: One handle — sit facing the anchor, pull one elbow to the ribs, no swing. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

exercises.name: Rayofi Lat Pulldown (kneeling, one arm)
exercises.cue: One handle, one Rayofi — anchor high via the door anchor, kneel, pull one elbow down and out, squeeze the lat. Left then right back to back — the other side is the rest. Pause only after both, not between sides.

cardioProtocol.context: Why this exists at all: July on the road ran 8,000+ steps a day and dropped the most weight of any month. Zone 2 is the deliberate version of that — the part that does not depend on the day going well.

zone2.note: at 4 km/h lands around ~100 bpm — Zone 1, too low
zone2.appleWatchSetup: Workout → Indoor Walk → ... → Heart Rate → Range 106-124 bpm, vibrates on drift
zone2.eveningRule: after 20:00 Zone 1 only (under 100 bpm) — Zone 2 late disrupts sleep
zone2.adhdBonus: even 100 bpm rhythmic walking regulates dopamine/noradrenaline — never wasted

stepTarget.parkingHack: park on the residential street before the destination rather than the lot — about a 5 min walk each way, same spot every time, no detour. ~1800 steps round trip, ~9000/week
stepTarget.badWeather: park in the lot — no penalty rule
stepTarget.evening: pad during show/podcast, Zone 1, effortless NEAT
stepTarget.why: +3000 steps/day ≈ 200-250 kcal without compensation — bigger lever than the weight gap alone

philipp.primaryRule: start low in rep range (e.g. 12), climb over weeks to 15 across all sets, then raise load and drop back to 12. Side delt target: clean 15 → 6kg. Pulldown/row/chest: +2.5kg when all sets hit top of range. RIR 2 non-negotiable.
philipp.maintenanceRule: 2 sets, same weight as last time, RIR 3, never progress — one number, no decision
philipp.missedSessionRule: never two in a row. One missed session is life, two is a pattern. Friday's shared Rayofi session is the safety net — minimum 1x/week structurally guaranteed.
philipp.deload: every 6-8 weeks, 1 light week at ~60%. Err earlier if sleep or appetite go off — cortisol is the enemy of muscle retention.

eunice.primaryRule: form before load; on glutes she can push closer to failure (RIR 1-2)
eunice.mindMuscle: squeeze and hold at the top of every rep — feeling the muscle matters more than the number
eunice.formFirst: a clean rep beats a heavy one you don't feel in the target muscle
eunice.deload: every 8 weeks, 1 light week — needed less often than Philipp since she's building, not cutting

_gaps: Sessions still duplicate exercise objects instead of referencing exercises.json by id
Every Rayofi load is unset — both people, every shared and optional session. Nothing to progress from until the device has actually been used once.
Hip Thrust (Dumbbell or Sandbag) has no demo video; it replaced the glute drive machine on 2026-08-29. None of the Rayofi or eGym entries have one either, and no video exists to link for them yet.

No warm-up anywhere in this file — zero sessions describe one. The gym Full Body opens on a lateral raise and reaches a 42.5 kg row by the fourth exercise, which wants a ramp set. Adding one is a training decision, not a data fix.
Eunice's Monday is recorded as 'eGym' with no station list, because the machines pick and progress the resistance themselves. Nothing about that session is trackable here, by design.

build_workout_page.py inlines this file without stripping _-prefixed keys, so these notes ship inside the public page even though nothing renders them — the same leak CLAUDE.md documents for four of the five builders.

_why.fullBodyNotSplit: At 2-3 sessions a week a push/pull split hits each muscle roughly once, which is the worst of both worlds. That is the whole reason the split was dropped in September 2026 — not that the old sessions were badly written.
_why.jointGymSessions: Training together at one station was never the problem; he said it worked. What failed was the old Friday plan, which gave them five shared exercises and then split into different tails, so they started together and had to separate halfway. A joint session works if the list is genuinely identical.
_why.homeIsPerPerson: Home is not a shared session. Each of them does their own session there when the weather stops the gym trip; Friday's Rayofi session is the only genuinely shared one at home. If both are rained out the same day they take turns on the one unit.
_why.travelIsShared: Travel is the opposite — always one shared session, both of them, same exercises, swapping during rest, because there is only one Rayofi to pack.
_why.oneRayofi: They own exactly one Rayofi Go-Tone Pro. Anything that would be a wide-bar two-hand pull at the gym goes one arm at a time, with per-side rep counts; the rear delt pull-apart is the exception, which is what the second cable handle is for. When both train at once they take turns and the rest period is the swap. Every load is marked '· start' because none of them has been measured on the device — see rayofiStartingLoads for where each number came from. The 30 kg ceiling only realistically bites on his one-arm lat pulldown.
_why.eunicesMonday: eGym, always, and recorded as a single line rather than a station list: the machines pick and progress their own resistance, so there is nothing here to plan a load or a set count for. Reconstructing it as individual exercises would be invention.
_why.conferenceWeeks: His Tuesday gym day moves to Wednesday on conference weeks. Nothing else shifts.
_why.rayofiStartingLoads: Now written into the sessions rather than kept here, because a number he cannot see while standing at the device is no use. Philipp's are derived from his MacroFactor workout log (Aug 2026 cable sets): lateral raise 5 kg transfers directly since it was already logged single-arm; row and pulldown are roughly 55% of his two-handed loads; face pull 10 kg and crunch 20 kg transfer near enough; biceps curl 7 kg is half of the 15 kg he did two-armed on a straight bar. Eunice has no workout export, so hers are conservative guesses to climb from, not derived. Everything is marked '· start' and should be replaced with real numbers after the first session. The stack figures they came from are not force at the handle, which is what the Rayofi reads.
_why.sessionLength: First real Rayofi session ran 70 minutes and four exercises still went undone, against a 45-60 minute target. Cause was the single-arm work: three exercises at three sets a side is 18 of the 32 bouts, and the implied pattern was left, rest, right, rest. Two fixes, no volume cut. Sides now run back to back with one rest after the pair, which removes about twelve minutes and actually gives each arm more recovery, not less. And the order is grouped by anchor height rather than by muscle priority, because on a single unit each re-anchor costs what walking to the next station costs at a gym — roughly three anchor changes now instead of seven. Realistic result is 50-55 minutes, not the 44 first estimated: that figure undercounted the rests on the single-arm sets. A second Rayofi would allow genuinely two-handed pulls, but on one motor both hands share the same 30 kg, so going two-handed would halve the load per arm exactly where he is closest to the ceiling.
_why.timePoorDesign: Cut on 2026-09-09 after the first real Rayofi session ran 70 minutes against a 45-60 target and four exercises went undone anyway — he had already voted with his feet on which ones were expendable. The rule applied: at two or three sessions a week the maintenance tier is what gets bought back as time. Triceps and the light squat go because the chest press and the gym leg press already cover them; core holds go because they are the one thing that genuinely can be done outside a session. What survives is the four taper drivers, one press, one posterior movement. Anything that needs no anchor now runs inside another exercise's rest rather than owning a slot. Each session also names its own minimum — the first two or three exercises — so a collapsed week still produces the part that matters instead of nothing.
_why.fridayPairing: The shared session is not a compromise: four of the five exercises are primary for both of them, because a wider shoulder and a broader back serve his taper and her shoulder-to-hip ratio equally. The hip thrust was the one asymmetry, originally solved by dose — her three heavy sets against his two light maintenance ones. Changed 2026-09-09 to drop his entirely: he gets hip extension at the gym twice a week anyway, glute mass works against the taper, and the minutes were being spent waiting. He now does the rear delt pull-apart during her hip thrusts and she does hers during his pulls — it needs no anchor, so it never occupies the device or a slot of its own.
